before: An instructor who has built a feedback prompt from an assignment, its rubric and examples of their own comments, following a published teaching guide, tests it before students see it. Each draft goes to the configured assistant in a fresh conversation, and the instructor tallies, for every planted problem, whether the feedback caught it, missed it or described it inaccurately, and also notes any comment naming a problem the draft does not have. The tally is read against a recent systematic review of classroom studies, which reports that language-model feedback supported revision for linguistic accuracy while human feedback remained stronger on higher-order issues, and whose authors regard designs in which teachers mediate the feedback as the most promising. The instructor revises the prompt, retests the drafts that exposed gaps, and saves the version that works best.
